ground_truth.primary_dx_title: Hydronephrosis with renal and ureteral calculous obstruction
ground_truth.primary_icd_title: Hydronephrosis with renal and ureteral calculous obstruction

diagnosis.llm_reason: The physician discharge diagnosis is nephrolithiasis (a complex right ureteropelvic junction stone >2cm). No rank in the differential names urolithiasis/kidney stone or obstructive uropathy. Ranks 1-5 (acute kidney injury, anemia, hematuria, nephrostomy tube pain, fever) are complications, associated findings, or symptoms that can accompany an obstructing renal calculus, but none is the same principal condition. Hematuria and AKI are downstream manifestations, not the stone disease itself.
diagnosis.llm_expanded_ground_truth: nephrolithiasis | kidney stone | renal calculus | ureteropelvic junction (UPJ) stone | staghorn/complex calculus >2cm | urolithiasis | obstructing renal stone with hydronephrosis

icd_linked.llm_icd_reason: No matching rank, so no mapped ICD to compare. The billed primary code N13.2 (hydronephrosis with renal and ureteral calculous obstruction) is not clinically equivalent to N17.9 (acute kidney failure), D64.9, R31.9, R52, or R50.9, which are symptom/complication codes rather than obstructive calculous disease codes.
